title: Best AI & Machine Learning Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare Duck.ai, Brave Leo and Startpage Anonymous View on how well they keep your chats, identity and data away from AI providers and model training.
intro: AI tools like ChatGPT collect massive amounts of personal data for training and improvement. Your conversations, uploads, and interactions may be stored indefinitely. These privacy-focused tools help protect your data from AI surveillance and unwanted collection.

verdict.summary: Duck.ai scores highest on this table: it needs no account, doesn't store chats by default, removes your IP address before a prompt reaches the model provider, and DuckDuckGo says those providers don't train on your chats. The most capable models need a paid subscription. Brave Leo comes next, with similar protections built into the Brave browser. Startpage Anonymous View hides your IP address from the sites you open, but it can't stop an AI service storing or training on what you type, so it scores low here.

pro_tips: Always use a VPN when accessing AI platforms to prevent IP-based tracking and data correlation across sessions.
Clear your browser cookies and local storage after AI sessions to prevent cross-site tracking and data persistence.
Avoid uploading personal documents or sensitive information to any AI platform, even privacy-focused ones.
Use temporary email addresses when AI platforms require registration to prevent linking to your real identity.
Regularly check AI platform privacy settings and opt out of data collection and model training where possible.

faqs.question: Can AI platforms still track me if I use private browsing mode?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private browsing only stops your own device keeping history and cookies after you close the window. The AI service still sees your IP address, can fingerprint your browser, and knows who you are if you sign in. A chat service that needs no account and removes your IP address before the prompt reaches the model, such as Duck.ai, limits what can be linked to you; Brave Leo also works without an account.

faqs.question: Is my ChatGPT conversation history really used to train AI models?
faqs.answer: By default, consumer ChatGPT can use your conversations to improve OpenAI's models unless you turn that off in settings, and Temporary Chats are kept for up to 30 days. Duck.ai doesn't store chats by default, and DuckDuckGo says its model providers don't use them for training.

faqs.question: How can I opt out of AI training data collection?
faqs.answer: In ChatGPT, open Settings > Data Controls and turn off 'Improve the model for everyone'. For other services, check the privacy or data settings, or ask support. Tools that don't use chats for training by design, such as Duck.ai and Brave Leo, don't need the setting.

faqs.question: Are there any completely anonymous AI chat options?
faqs.answer: Nothing is fully anonymous if you type identifying details into a chat. Duck.ai and Brave Leo come closest among the tools here: neither needs an account, and both say they don't store chats or use them for training. Duck.ai also removes your IP address before a prompt reaches the model provider.

faqs.question: What data do AI platforms typically collect besides conversations?
faqs.answer: AI platforms collect IP addresses, device information, usage patterns, timestamps, uploaded files, and often link this to your account profile. They may also track which features you use and how often to improve their services and target advertising.
